title: Gunpowder Plot & Glorious Revolution Adventure
welcome_lead: It's the Stuart age. Catch Guy Fawkes in the cellars in 1605, then watch a king flee in 1688. 💣
meta_desc: Stuart Britain Adventure — a KS3 walkthrough of the Gunpowder Plot 1605 and the Glorious Revolution 1688.
final_note: You met Guy Fawkes and the 1605 plot, then saw how 1688 brought William and Mary in and Catholic James II out.

concepts.def: First Stuart king of England, from 1603
Catholic plan to blow up Parliament

walkthroughs.body_html:
After Elizabeth I died in 1603, her cousin James I of Scotland became king of England too.

James was Protestant, and Catholics were treated badly. A small group of Catholic gentlemen, led by Robert Catesby, planned to blow up Parliament on 5 November 1605.

Guy Fawkes was caught in the cellars with 36 barrels of gunpowder. He was tortured and executed. 🎆

The Stuart kings often argued with Parliament over money and religion.

James I's son Charles I fought a Civil War with Parliament — and was executed in 1649. After 11 years without a king (the Commonwealth), the throne was given back to Charles II in 1660 — called the Restoration.

But the next king, James II, was Catholic — and many in England were not happy.

In 1688 Parliament invited James II's Protestant daughter Mary and her Dutch husband William of Orange to take the throne.

William sailed over with an army. James II ran away to France with hardly a shot fired — which is why people called it the Glorious Revolution.

In 1689 the new monarchs accepted the Bill of Rights, which limited royal power and gave Parliament a bigger role. 🇬🇧

mcqs.q: On what date did the Gunpowder Plot fail?
Who became king after Elizabeth I?
How did Anglo-Saxons come to dominate post-Roman Britain?
options: The Ripper was caught but his name was kept secret to protect the Royal Family.
Anglo-Saxons came as refugees fleeing the Vikings.
Anglo-Saxons invaded Britain and wiped out all the Romano-British inhabitants.
A mix of migration from northern Germany and Denmark, settlement and intermarriage, and cultural absorption of Romano-British populations — not simple invasion and replacement.

mcqs.q: Why were the Whitechapel murders never solved?
options: The Ripper was caught but his name was kept secret to protect the Royal Family.
Anglo-Saxons came as refugees fleeing the Vikings.
The police failed to solve the murders because they didn't try hard enough.
Lack of forensic techniques, no fingerprinting or DNA, conflicting witness accounts, jurisdictional confusion between forces, and possibly police incompetence and media interference.
